before: Tables refused cell merge and split, and column edits on tables with merged cells. A child adopted by a removed node whose survivor was removed again showed nowhere.
after: Merge and split rebuild one table with existing tree primitives; moved paragraphs keep their identity, and a lower cell whose content moves is replaced by a fresh continuation cell. Adoption follows a chain of survivors to the last live one.
reason: The operations write only putNode, setAttribute and spliceChildren effects that released readers apply the same way. Chain adoption reads the existing replacedBy and deleted fields transitively. A released reader hides a child adopted through a chain, which is the case it already lost, until any participant edits that cell and lists the child there explicitly.
